sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
The ledgerlite tests pass with this command, run from the project root (`<run>\work\L1\c\w`):

```
PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

It ran 2 tests and both passed (`test_transfer_preserves_total` and `test_rejects_non_positive_amount`).

The `PYTHONPATH=src` part is needed because the `ledgerlite` package is in `src/` and the project has no packaging config (no `pyproject.toml` or `setup.py`). Without it, the tests can't import `ledgerlite`. The tests use only the standard library `unittest`, so there was nothing to install. I used the system Python 3.13.15 and made no changes to any files.

In PowerShell or cmd, set the variable separately. In PowerShell that's `$env:PYTHONPATH="src"; python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`.

sessions.name: B
sessions.reply:
I added `Ledger.close(name)` in `src/ledgerlite/__init__.py`. It raises `ValueError` if the account's balance isn't zero. Otherwise it removes the account. Closing an account that doesn't exist raises `KeyError`, the same as `balance()` does.

I added `test_close_requires_zero_balance` in `tests/test_ledger.py`. It checks that a non-zero account is refused and stays in the ledger, and that it can be closed once the balance is back to zero.

The full suite passes: 3 tests, all OK.
